items.title: Joe Ascione interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: He said, “He’s played with Blakey and Elvin and Buddy Rich” and this and this.

ctx.x: So I always knew of him and Charlie Perry always used to say see if you can get to hook up with Billy. It never happened until a couple of years later, Sonny’s Jazz Club on Long Island had Billy do a Wednesday night steady gig for a while. And somehow I got the call from Sonny, the owner. And he said, “Hey, Joe” real raspy voice, scotch-ladened voice, you know “Joey, baby, come on here and play with Billy.” And I was nervous. So I’m sitting there and it’s I think Wes Belcamp and Pete Chivoli who used to play with…

drummer, play the drums.” All right. So I walk in the house, in the place, scratching my head. I see Mark Elf, you’re the drummer, play the drums. I say, “Mark, what the hell’s this guy talking about? You’re the drummer, play the drums?” He said, “Man you can’t kick those tubs hard enough.” He said, “He’s played with Blakey and Elvin and Buddy Rich” and this and this. He said, “Just go, man, hit ‘em.” All right. Next set so I boom- boom, start bashing. “Yeah, yeah, all right.” And by the end of that set he turned…
Yeah. I like the way that the older fellas have a succinct way of telling you what they want.
